messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Cross-region routing error spike: 5xx rate increased from 0.2% -> 8% for eu-west. Trigger: routing-policy mismatch checks. Pager sent to #incidents and oncall.
Alice M.: seeing reproducible 502s hitting eu-west -> backend-a variants. TTL on geo-pin is 30s, but probes show mixed region responses.
Ben K.: I can confirm logs show requests routed to us-east instances even when geo-pin weight=100 for eu-west. Suspect route policy conversion bug after recent rollout.
Carla S.: tagging the deployment that rolled yesterday: infra/routing v3.14. Deployed 02:10 UTC. Rollback candidate prepared.
Dan (oncall): taking lead. Paging support and SRE. Running initial impact assessment. @Support Lead please surface any customer-reported incidents.
Support Lead: flagged 6 customers with elevated errors; one enterprise customer (acme-inc) reporting 30% of requests failing in EU. CS is on a call.
Dan (oncall): quick mitigation plan: 1) pin eu-west to previous routing-policy snapshot (v3.13) 2) increase DNS TTL to 60s to prevent rapid oscillation 3) enable fallback to local replicas. Executing step 1 now.
Ben K.: rollback command: `./routingctl promote-snapshot --region eu-west --snapshot v3.13 --force`
Dan (oncall): ran promote-snapshot, got `OK` but metrics still show some east-bound traffic. KVs show mixed policy states across control-plane pods.
Alice M.: running probe from probe-runner: `curl -H \"x-region:eu-west\" https://probe.redwood/api/health` -> returns 502 intermittently, source shows us-east backends.
Eugene R.: I see an operator race in control-plane reconciliation logs: controller processed both rollout and pin-change messages concurrently, last-write-wins led to wrong policy on subset of nodes. Patch queued.
Carla S.: patch: adding a compare-and-swap on policy apply to avoid race. Small hotfix PR ready. Recommend canary apply to small AZ first.
Dan (oncall): immediate next steps: revert to safe pins where possible and scale up eu-west control-plane to force state convergence. Initiating scale command.
Ben K.: scaled control-plane replicas from 3 -> 6 in eu-west. Watching convergence.
Alice M.: after scale, 5xx rate dropped to ~1.2% in last 2m. TCP traces show remaining misroutes are from DNS caching at some edge providers.
Support Lead: CS confirms acme-inc errors down to ~5% after mitigation. They request RCA and postmortem.
Dan (oncall): longer-term: roll back routing rollout, add stricter operator locks, and add automated audit that detects mismatched pin weight vs applied state. Filing incident ticket: INC-2026-172842.
Eugene R.: hotfix merged, will deploy after canary. Also increasing default pin TTL to 300s as a precaution while we review policy propagation semantics.
Carla S.: deploying canary to eu-west-a only (`infra/routing v3.14+hotfix`). Monitoring for 10m.
incident-bot: deploybot: canary deploy started (eu-west-a) by Carla S.
Ben K.: canary looks clean for 8m, no 502s from that AZ. Proceeding with staggered rollout to other AZs.
Dan (oncall): handoff: I will update on-call schedule and postmortem owner (Alice) in 30m. Closing page once we see stable <0.5% 5xx for 15m.
Support Lead: sending comms to affected customers: mitigation applied, we are monitoring, follow-up RCA ETA 24h. :thumbsup:
Alice M.: noted as incident lead for postmortem. Will include timeline, root cause (control-plane operator race), customer impact, and follow-up actions.
Dan (oncall): incident resolved for now — 5xx at 0.18% over 20m. Closing page. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: [RESOLVED] INC-2026-172842 closed by Dan (oncall)
